findings.situation: A couple files jointly for 2025, but the spouse filed a separate 2024 return whose Form 4952 shows an amount on line 7, and the filer reads "Do you have ... your 2024 Form 4952" as asking only about their own return.
findings.source_text: f4952 p. 1, Part I, line 2: "Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7"
findings.why: The joint 2025 Form 4952 line 2 must include the spouse's 2024 carryforward. The gate explicitly says "by either of you, on a joint or separate return," but this question says only "you" and "your 2024 Form 4952" and never mentions the spouse, so the filer may truthfully answer no.

findings.situation: A filer's investment interest was first disallowed in 2022 and carried through 2024 Form 4952 lines 2 and 7 into 2025, and the filer is unsure whether that counts as "disallowed in 2024."
findings.source_text: f4952 p. 1, line 7: "Disallowed investment interest expense to be carried forward"; line 2: "Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7"
findings.why: "Investment interest expense that was disallowed in 2024" can be read as only interest first disallowed in 2024, which would exclude older carryforwards that 2024 line 7 includes. The parenthetical reference to line 7 points the other way. The two readings give different yes/no answers for line 2.

locators: p. 1, Part I, line 2, "Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7"
p. 1, Part I, line 2, "Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7"; p. 3, Who Must File, "You don’t have any carryover of disallowed investment interest expense from 2024"

findings.situation: A filer holds a partnership or S corporation interest whose Schedule K-1 reports investment interest expense, but the filer did not borrow any money personally.
findings.source_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Include investment interest expense reported to you on Schedule K-1 from a partnership or an S corporation."
findings.why: The question asks only about interest the filer or spouse paid on money they borrowed, and the help mentions only broker margin statements. A truthful filer would leave out K-1 investment interest, which line 1 must include.

findings.situation: A filer accrued investment interest in 2025 but did not pay it in 2025.
findings.source_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Enter the investment interest expense paid or accrued during the tax year"
findings.why: The question asks only for interest paid, so accrued but unpaid investment interest is left out of the answer.

findings.situation: A filer borrowed to buy a working interest in an oil or gas property with unlimited liability and did not materially participate, and does not see it as 'investments'.
findings.source_text: f4952 p. 3, Property held for investment: "A working interest in an oil or gas property that you held directly or through an entity that didn't limit your liability is property held for investment, but only if you didn't materially participate"
findings.why: An ordinary filer would see an oil or gas working interest as a business, not as 'investments', and might leave it out. The text counts it as property held for investment, so its interest belongs on line 1.

findings.situation: A filer borrowed money to buy a rental property or an interest in a passive partnership, which they think of as an investment, and reports that interest.
findings.source_text: Question: "pay in 2025 on money borrowed to buy investments? Leave out interest on money used to buy, build or improve your home, and on money that went into tax-exempt bonds or a business." vs f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Investment interest expense doesn't include ... Interest expense that is properly allocable to a passive activity ... any rental activity"
findings.why: The list of things to leave out does not mention rentals or passive activities. Filers usually call a rental property an 'investment', so that interest would wrongly go on line 1.

findings.situation: A filer borrowed against a life insurance or annuity contract issued after June 8, 1997 to buy stocks, or paid capitalized construction interest on land held for investment, and reports that interest.
findings.source_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Any interest expense that is capitalized, such as construction interest subject to section 263A" and "Interest expense, disallowed under section 264 ... even if the proceeds were used to purchase any property held for investment"
findings.why: The question does not tell the filer to leave out capitalized interest or interest disallowed under section 264. Both meet the question's 'money borrowed to buy investments' wording but are excluded from line 1.
